"Flippy" The Burger-Flipping Robot Taken Offline After First Day

Flippy is a constraint in the burger making process. In manufacturing, the flow of work is dictated by the most constrained step. If Flippy cannot be fed prepared patties when it needs them or cannot provide enough cooked patties when they are required, then Flippy is the limiting factor in the process. Since Flippy is a one trick pony and cannot readily adapt to changing situations, then this robot is a true bottleneck and will disrupt flow. You cannot just have Flippy make patties at its maximum constrained rate since that would mean waste during slow sales periods, but it also cannot handle peaks periods either since it relies on upstream and downstream workers to maintain its pace. The Theory of Constraints model of manufacturing could help with this, but ultimately I cannot see Flippy becoming a seamless part of the process. A second human cook could jump in much more easily and effectively in a peak period and then go back to other duties when demand drops. Hell, a single human can do the whole process by themselves, albeit at reduced efficiency, but it is possible (I worked a burger flipping job in high school and often had to do it all when we had only two people on the clock). In the end, Flippy will be no more an aid than any other tool in the kitchen that limits the rate at which you can produce. It's something we've already seen time and time again in manufacturing so don't get too excited about the idea of a robot doing a better job than a human in making food. You're stuck with the low-wage, low-IQ, no-care fast food drones for the foreseeable future.
